No problem particularly running the apps, but storing them was the problem. Here, today, though, the problem is that the apps have become so out-of-control bloated - once the device OEMs woke up and realized "oh, we should put more storage in there" - that they each act like the only app on your phone. They have triggers that keep components running in the background (Spotify, Pandora, Facebook, etc. have huge "Service" processes you can't stop... and don't even get me started on Google's services!). Under "app poverty", the more apps you install, the less you can get done.

Also, though, if I have an app that is particularly memory intensive (say, a game, or a large PDF), then the app itself will be quite slow and non-responsive. I have had a few "Force Close" incidents as well that I attribute mostly to lack of memory. As an addendum, I also learned after-the-fact that the version with amazon ads is the only version of these phones that cannot be "jail broken" for installing custom android versions. This actually makes sense in retrospect, as I would likely be able to remove the ads feature if I did this. I thought I would include this, though, for anyone else that is interested in "rooting" their device. The inability to jail brake the device, though, has not contributed to my 2-star rating

Solid phone at a solid price.. Purchased this after my beloved Moto X Pure suffered a cracked screen. Absolutely no complaints so far. I highly recommend going with the 4GB of ram over the 2 GB model. I can open multiple apps and it handles it without a hiccup. Battery life is better than any phone that I have previously owned and the Turbo charger gives me a quick charge when I need it. It's about as stock Android as you're going to find without buying a Pixel 2. It is already slated to receive the Oreo update, although Lenovo is usually a little slower than most with making updates available. All in all, I'm very satisfied with this phone, as well as the Moto X Pure that I previously owned.
Excellent MOTO!. This phone is everything I thought it would be. Great pictures, apps, speed, etc. It is well worth the money!

Lots of calls, Facebook, email, you tube, various productivity apps... etc. I can go pretty much 3 days between charges and when it needs it, the phone charges fast. My old Lumia needed to be charged frequently even when it was new and every night the iPhone and the Samsung Galaxy in my house are on their chargers or they are both bricks the next day. Not the Moto G Plus, but excellent batter life comes with some big tradeoffs. Processor speed. This is a harder one for me to evaluate since I was upgrading from a phone that was a couple generations old and running an antiquated OS, but this phone seems fast. I surf along with others in the family using higher end phones and don't seem to be noticeably behind and the performance well outpaces what I upgraded from. Size and dimensions.

Best of the mid-range phones, a King has come!. Bought on another e-tailer site on a Black Friday deal. This is the second one I've bought, previous was purchased from a big blue box retailer. I migrated from a Samusung Galaxy S5 on the Verizon network. Pros: You're not going to get a better performer at this price point. Long battery life, snappy performance, stock android (no bloatware), and service unlocked (works well on Verizon). 64gb storage to avoid "forced obsolescence", 4gb RAM, and an EXCELLENT fingerprint reader, better than the S5 even!. Love the "Moto Actions" app that allows the home / fingerprint reader button to act as a "back" and "active apps" button as well, giving more room on screen for apps by eliminating those from the display. Most Verizon apps still work (Message+, Visual Voicemail), except "My Verizon".

What I found are, relative to the iPhone, are: it does not focus as accurately and often missed focusing on people in photos, the shutter lag is very long, it does not do well in lower light situations, it can't handle backlit scenes very well, photos were generally darker lacking detail in shadows, and takes a very long time to save panorama photos. I actually ended up carrying my iPhone with me to take photos and only used the Moto if I wanted to immediately send the photo to someone. So, if you are a photo oriented person - I would be careful with this phone.

Primarily, the lack of speedy updates. Most Android developers seem to miss this mark, though (aside from Google itself), so it seems more of an Android thing than a Moto/Lenovo thing. It's very likely the G5+ will get at least Android O at some point, albeit a bit later than most would like. Still, it would be nice to see Lenovo follow up on their initial promises to get faster updates out. Other issues are a glitchy light sensor (seems to not always brighten up when it should), a tweaky sleep/daydream mode (I've seen it stay awake past the set timer for no reason, but this seems rather rare), and, as of August 2017, a glitchy Google app that freezes up sometimes (though this is really Google's fault, as it wasn't always this way according to reviews and others who have had the phone longer).

I don't play games on my phone so I can't say whether it's good for that, but Spotify, YouTube and various social media apps work very well. Amazon Ads are not very intrusive, and if you want you can have apps (like Weather Channel) that have persistent notifications and it keeps the ads from covering your whole screen, it essentially turns them into a notification. I can't wait to see Motorola's next G device, this one has made me a big fan.

Also, though, if I have an app that is particularly memory intensive (say, a game, or a large PDF), then the app itself will be quite slow and non-responsive. I have had a few "Force Close" incidents as well that I attribute mostly to lack of memory. As an addendum, I also learned after-the-fact that the version with amazon ads is the only version of these phones that cannot be "jail broken" for installing custom android versions. That were more pronounced at photos, interface colors are basically fine. SIM card was recognized as soon as it was inserted without the reboot. The overall performance seems to be fine. Pros: Battery life is phenomenal, finger print reader and its one button navigation is my favorite, HD screen is really good, Camera is excellent for most (80%) shooting situations with good-moderate light and relatively steady objects, Video is also good enough for everyday use. Processed speed and multiple applications are not a problem, unless you play intensive HD games while opening 10 other apps. Cons: Low light performance is a problem, but passable with flash. No optical image stabilization so you can't take fast moving objects. It can't take good pictures of your Formula 1 or Indy races, but expecting these things in a $200 smart phone requires you to visit a psychiatrist. Carry a DSLR or a good pocket megazoom if you really want top notch photos or spend $700 and get an iPhone or S8.

No need to contact anyone at T-mobile, manually set APNs, etc. Some things I particularly appreciate: - clean, near-stock Android 7.0 Nougat, like a Nexus or Pixel, without having to mess with third-party ROMs - no bloat, no Touchwiz, EMUI or other clunky skins. I did install Nova Launcher to stop Google Now from taking over my "swipe-left" home screen. - excellent performance in common apps. I don't play 3D action games, and so can't address those. With 4GB, 8 cores, and internal flash memory that seems faster than average, there's no lag even when rapidly switching between several large apps. Heavy multi-taskers should definitely spring for the 4GB model, and budget permitting, I'd recommend the same to anyone hoping to keep their G5+ for more than a couple of years, just for future-proofing.
